jobs.title: Sr. Director, Cybersecurity Advisory Services
jobs.description:
Presidio, Where Teamwork and Innovation Shape the Future

At Presidio, we're at the forefront of a global technology revolution, transforming industries through cutting-edge digital solutions and next-generation AI. We empower businesses - and their internal customers - to achieve more through innovation, automation, and intelligent insights.

The Role

As a Senior Cybersecurity Consulting Leader with Presidio, you will be responsible for scaling an established Cyber Consulting Services organization and growing the business faster than market pace. You will lead Information Security Governance, Cybersecurity Architecture, and Offensive Security while owning the operating performance of the consulting portfolio. You will be accountable for revenue growth, gross profit and margin, utilization, delivery quality, backlog, capacity, and workforce strategy. You will lead through managers and principal consultants while maintaining technical and client credibility to challenge how the practice delivers, scales, and evolves.

Travel Requirements

This is a client-facing role. You will be required to travel up to 30% to client locations to deliver professional services when needed.

Responsibilities Include

Lead a distributed Cyber Consulting Services organization spanning Information Security Governance, Cybersecurity Architecture, and Offensive Security.
Grow the business faster than the cybersecurity services market while maintaining expectations for gross profit, gross margin, utilization, delivery quality, and client outcomes.
Own operating performance across revenue, GP/GM, utilization, backlog, capacity, project economics, delivery forecasting, and engagement health.
Build workforce plans that balance FTE capacity, skills, backlog, utilization, projected demand, and consulting economics.
Increase internally delivered services revenue by building FTE capability and using subcontractors selectively for specialized skills or capacity requirements.
Own subcontractor and third-party delivery strategy, including partner selection, economics, quality, capacity, performance, and appropriate use.
Lead, develop, and hold accountable managers responsible for consulting teams and individual contributors across multiple cybersecurity disciplines.
Own succession planning, leadership development, performance management, hiring strategy, career development, and retention across the consulting organization.
Establish operating mechanisms for resource forecasting, engagement governance, project reviews, quality control, utilization management, and delivery escalations.
Maintain executive oversight of major consulting engagements and intervene when delivery quality, project economics, client satisfaction, or contractual commitments are at risk.
Create, evolve, and retire consulting services based on client demand, delivery performance, market changes, technical developments, and the ability to scale delivery.
Define and improve consulting methodologies, delivery standards, costing models, level-of-effort models, and repeatable engagement structures.
Challenge Principal-level consultants and practice leaders on technical direction, methodology, service relevance, delivery quality, and opportunities to develop new capabilities.
Partner with Client Success Management, Sales, and pre-sales teams on strategic engagements, capacity requirements, client needs, and technical sales enablement.
Develop technical enablement that helps Sales and pre-sales teams identify, position, and qualify appropriate cybersecurity consulting opportunities.
Engage CISOs, CIOs, CTOs, and other executives during strategic engagements, client escalations, executive briefings, and consulting sponsorship activities.
Build collaboration across governance, architecture, and offensive security teams so clients can access integrated consulting capabilities rather than isolated technical services.

Required Skills And Professional Experience

Bachelor’s degree or the equivalent work experience and/or military experience
Minimum of 12-15 years of cybersecurity experience with progressively increasing leadership responsibility.
Significant leadership experience in cybersecurity consulting, advisory, professional services, or a comparable client-facing security organization.
Demonstrated experience leading managers as well as senior individual contributors, with experience operating geographically distributed teams of more than 20 people.
Experience leading a multi-disciplinary cybersecurity organization that includes governance, security architecture, offensive security, or comparable consulting disciplines.
Demonstrated financial accountability for a consulting or professional services organization, including revenue, margin, utilization, capacity, and project economics.
Experience managing project-based consulting delivered through fixed-fee, T&M, retainer, or comparable professional services models.
Ability to work effectively with Sales and pre-sales organizations without compromising the independence and risk-based approach of a vendor-neutral consulting practice.
Functional understanding of relevant regulations and industry standards (e.g., SOX, AICPA SOC Reporting Standards, ISO27001, PCI, NIST, HIPAA) and best practices and methodologies to address these requirements.
Experience developing workforce plans that balance permanent employees, demand, utilization, specialized skills, and external delivery capacity.
Experience managing subcontractors or third-party delivery resources while maintaining internal delivery capability as the primary foundation for growth.
Experience working directly with senior client executives and serving as an escalation point or executive sponsor for complex cybersecurity engagements.
Ability to manage consulting economics using revenue, gross profit, gross margin, utilization, backlog, capacity, forecasting, and project-level financial performance.
Strong understanding of cybersecurity consulting across GRC, security architecture, offensive security, application security, and cloud security.
Technical depth sufficient to challenge Principal Consultants on methodologies, technical approaches, service design, delivery quality, and emerging client requirements.
Ability to translate consulting demand and backlog into FTE hiring, development, subcontractor, and capacity decisions.
Demonstrated ability to improve utilization and margin without compromising delivery quality or creating unsustainable workloads.
Experience building repeatable consulting services, including methodology, scope, level-of-effort estimates, costing, staffing models, and delivery standards.
Ability to identify when consulting services should be expanded, redesigned, standardized, or retired based on performance and market demand.
Demonstrated success building collaborative teams across distinct technical disciplines and developing managers who can lead experienced practitioners.
Executive communication skills sufficient to advise and challenge senior client stakeholders and manage difficult delivery or commercial conversations.
Experience operating in a remote or geographically distributed delivery organization.
Ability to travel up to 30% for client engagements and internal meetings.

Preferred Skills And Professional Experience

Experience developing or scaling AI Security consulting capabilities or advising clients on security risks associated with enterprise AI adoption.
Experience leading service portfolio development, including launching new cybersecurity consulting offerings and retiring services that no longer meet business or client requirements.
Experience developing technical enablement for Sales and pre-sales teams to improve identification and qualification of consulting opportunities.
Experience speaking at cybersecurity conferences, client events, executive briefings, or other external forums.
CISSP, CISM, CISA, or comparable cybersecurity certification.
Bachelor's degree in cybersecurity, information technology, computer science, business, or a related field.
Military leadership or cybersecurity experience

You will advance AI-enabled operations and crisis readiness with Investigations, Threat Hunting & Forensics and enterprise partners.

Lead global CIRT operations, including follow-the-sun coverage, escalation, containment, recovery, closure, and continuity during outages.

Advance responsible AI-assisted triage, investigation, decision support, documentation, and response with oversight, approvals, auditability, and reversibility.

Direct incident response; govern non-destructive containment and automated actions; and engage Investigations, Threat Hunting & Forensics when required.

Lead executive briefings, stakeholder updates, reporting, communication cadence, and documentation of significant decisions.

Apply incident response, recovery, crisis communications, business continuity, and crisis coordination practices during high-pressure events.
Translate issues into business terms and coordinate concurrent workstreams using risk-based decisions.
Integrate FDA, HIPAA, SEC cyber disclosure, sanctions compliance, and other reporting considerations into response processes.
Address threats involving contractors and contingent workers through identity verification and access revocation coordination.

Translate technical findings, remediation status, and risk trends into clear written, verbal, and presentation-ready updates for technical and executive audiences.

Design secure hybrid and multi-cloud connectivity using Direct Connect, Interconnect, private endpoints, VPN, and transit architectures.

Ensure high availability, performance monitoring, and capacity planning for mission-critical clinical and patient-facing services.

Support infrastructure for manufacturing sites and clinical operations, including device and equipment connectivity where applicable.

Embed security by design across infrastructure through hardening baselines, secure configurations, and Infrastructure-as-Code guardrails.
Own timely vulnerability remediation and patching across infrastructure assets, meeting SLAs defined by the Security team.

Protect patient health information through appropriate data residency, encryption, access controls, and logging.

Title Open Rank (Lecturer Track) in Cybersecurity for Cyber-Physical Systems and Founding Program Director Appointment Status Non-Tenure Track Department IU Columbus Columbus Location Columbus Position Summary

Position Summary

The Division of Behavioral, Health, and Life Sciences at Indiana University Columbus invites applications for a full-time, open-rank non-tenure-track faculty position in Cybersecurity for Cyber-Physical Systems. The successful candidate will also receive an initial administrative assignment as Founding Program Director for the proposed B.S. in Cybersecurity for Cyber-Physical Systems
. The position reports to the Head of the Division of Behavioral, Health and Life Sciences.

The proposed 120-credit Bachelor of Science program is designed to prepare students to secure computing systems that monitor or control physical processes. jobs.description:
Position Overview

The IT Security Program Manager
is responsible for executing and managing the day-to-day operations of Recovery Centers of America's cybersecurity program. Reporting to the manager of infrastructure under the IT OPS director and ensures that RCA's security posture remains compliant with HIPAA, HITECH
, and NIST 800-53
standards while continuously improving the effectiveness of the organization's security controls and risk management framework.

This role will coordinate and perform audits, oversee third-party risk management, manage RCA's security awareness and phishing programs, drive policy governance, and ensure the timely resolution of open risk items and vulnerabilities. The ideal candidate is an organized, hands-on leader with a strong understanding of healthcare security and compliance who can align security initiatives with RCA's mission of saving one million lives.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Program Management & Governance

Manage the daily operations of RCA's cybersecurity program under the guidance of the CISO.
Coordinate and track the completion of internal and external security audits, including HIPAA, SOC 2, and NIST-based assessments.
Maintain and monitor the Information Security Risk Register, ensuring timely resolution of identified issues and mitigation of critical findings.
Lead tabletop exercises and incident response simulations to test and improve RCA's preparedness and business continuity planning.
Collaborate with RCA leadership and department heads to ensure that security policies and controls are understood and effectively implemented across all business units.

Third-Party Risk & Vendor Management

Manage the third-party risk assessment program, ensuring that all vendors with access to PHI or critical systems undergo security evaluation and periodic reassessment.
Review BAAs, security questionnaires, and compliance attestations; ensure corrective action for identified gaps.
Partner with Procurement and Legal to integrate security requirements into new and existing vendor contracts.

Policy, Compliance, and Reporting

Work with the CISO to review, update, and publish information security policies, standards, and procedures in accordance with HIPAA, HITECH, and NIST frameworks.
Develop dashboards and recurring reports to track security metrics, compliance posture, and program maturity for presentation to the CISO and executive leadership.
Monitor and interpret changes to regulatory requirements, ensuring timely updates to RCA's compliance program.

Security Awareness & Training

Administer and optimize RCA's KnowBe4 Security Awareness and Phishing Training Program.
Track user engagement and training completion rates, and provide metrics and recommendations to leadership.
Develop creative awareness campaigns to strengthen RCA's security culture.

Vulnerability & Infrastructure Management

Identify and track critical infrastructure vulnerabilities, working with IT and Infrastructure teams to ensure remediation and continuous monitoring.
Oversee MDM security, ensuring appropriate device controls, encryption, and enforcement of mobile security policies.
Support the CISO in analyzing threat intelligence, vulnerability trends, and endpoint security performance (e.g., CrowdStrike, firewall alerts).

Risk and Compliance Leadership

Ensure continuous compliance with HIPAA, HITECH, and NIST 800-53 / 800-171 requirements.
Coordinate with Compliance, Legal, and Clinical leadership to ensure consistent risk management practices.
Participate in post-incident reviews, documenting lessons learned and recommending process improvements.

Education

Bachelor's degree in Information Security, Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field required.

Experience

Minimum of 5--7 years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, IT risk management, or audit within a regulated environment (preferably healthcare).
At least 2 years in a program management or leadership role overseeing information security functions.
Strong working knowledge of HIPAA, NIST 800-53, HITRUST, and security risk management frameworks.

Certifications (preferred But Not Required)

Security +, CISSP, CISM, CRISC, HCISPP, or equivalent security certification.
PMP or similar project management certification is a plus.

Technical Skills

Understanding of endpoint protection, SIEM tools, MDM platforms (e.g., Intune), and vulnerability management solutions.
Experience with vendor risk tools, audit tracking systems, and compliance reporting.
Familiarity with Microsoft 365 Security Suite, KnowBe4, and GRC platforms.

Core Competencies

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical risks for non-technical stakeholders.
Highly organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
Demonstrated ability to build cross-functional relationships and drive accountability.
Passionate about RCA's mission and maintaining the privacy and security of patient information

Travel

Limited travel is required for this position
This position is primarily a remote position

new_jobs.title: Senior Director, Global Infrastructure Technology & Operations
new_jobs.description:
Career-defining. Life-changing.

At iRhythm, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your skills and your career while impacting the lives of people around the world. iRhythm is shaping a future where everyone, everywhere can access the best possible cardiac health solutions. Every day, we collaborate, create, and constantly reimagine what’s possible. We think big and move fast, driven by our commitment to put patients first and improve lives. We need builders like you. Curious and innovative problem solvers looking for the chance to meaningfully shape the future of cardiac health, our company, and your career

About This Role

The Senior Director, Global Infrastructure Technology & Operations will lead iRhythm’s enterprise infrastructure strategy, architecture, operations, and modernization across cloud, networking, data center and hardware, end-user computing, and security infrastructure. This role will ensure that iRhythm’s technology foundation is resilient, secure, compliant, and scalable enough to support 24/7 clinical operations, manufacturing, global commercial growth, and the company’s expanding data and AI capabilities. This senior leadership role combines executive leadership, hands-on technical depth, organizational development, financial stewardship, and close partnership with the Chief Data Officer and head of IT, CISO, Quality/Regulatory, Engineering, and business leaders. The role works hand in hand with the CISO: Security defines the requirements and provides oversight, while Infrastructure delivers and operates the platforms, controls, and services that enable the business.

What You Will Be Doing

Strategy & Leadership

Define and execute a multi-year enterprise infrastructure strategy and roadmap aligned to iRhythm’s business, clinical, data, and AI objectives.
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing infrastructure organization across cloud, network, operations, end-user services, and managed service partners.
Establish infrastructure architecture standards, reference patterns, governance, and operating models across business units and geographies.
Serve as the senior infrastructure advisor to executive leadership, translating strategy, risk, investment, and performance into business terms.

Cloud Infrastructure

Own the enterprise multi-cloud strategy across AWS, GCP, Azure, and Microsoft 365, including landing zones, account and project structure, identity integration, and guardrails.
Lead cloud platform engineering using Infrastructure as Code, automation, infrastructure CI/CD, and policy-as-code.
Drive FinOps practices, including cost visibility, optimization, reserved-capacity strategy, and chargeback/showback.
Enable modern data and AI platforms—including Snowflake, enterprise AI and search platforms, and ML/GPU workloads—with secure, scalable, well-governed infrastructure and private connectivity patterns.
Lead workload migration and modernization from on-premises environments to cloud where appropriate.

Networking & Connectivity

Own enterprise network architecture across corporate offices, clinical and IDTF sites, manufacturing facilities, data centers, and cloud environments, including LAN, WAN, SD-WAN, Wi-Fi, SASE, DNS, and load balancing.
Design secure hybrid and multi-cloud connectivity using Direct Connect, Interconnect, private endpoints, VPN, and transit architectures.
Implement network segmentation and isolation for manufacturing/OT and clinical environments in alignment with Zero Trust principles.
Ensure high availability, performance monitoring, and capacity planning for mission-critical clinical and patient-facing services.

Data Center, Hardware & End-User Computing

Oversee on-premises and colocation data centers, compute, storage, backup, and virtualization platforms, including lifecycle management and rationalization.
Own the hardware asset lifecycle, including procurement, standards, refresh cycles, and secure disposal.
Lead end-user computing across endpoints, MDM, collaboration tools, service desk, and conference room technology to deliver a secure and productive employee experience.
Support infrastructure for manufacturing sites and clinical operations, including device and equipment connectivity where applicable.
Security Infrastructure
Implement, operate, and maintain infrastructure security controls in alignment with the security strategy, policies, and standards set by the CISO.
Own the day-to-day engineering and operation of network and platform security technologies such as firewalls, WAF, proxies/SASE, NAC, and VPN, with the CISO’s team defining requirements, configuration standards, and monitoring.
Embed security by design across infrastructure through hardening baselines, secure configurations, and Infrastructure-as-Code guardrails.
Own timely vulnerability remediation and patching across infrastructure assets, meeting SLAs defined by the Security team.
Operate identity and directory infrastructure, including SSO, MFA, and directory services, in support of the CISO-led Zero Trust and identity roadmap.
Partner with the CISO’s organization during security incidents by providing infrastructure expertise, containment, remediation, logs, telemetry, and integrations needed for detection and response.

Compliance, Quality & Regulated Environments

Ensure infrastructure meets applicable regulatory and compliance obligations, including FDA QMSR (21 CFR Part 820), 21 CFR Part 11, HIPAA/HITECH, SOC 2, ISO 13485, ISO 27001, GDPR/UK GDPR, and other international requirements.
Partner with the CISO, Quality, and Regulatory teams to maintain infrastructure controls and evidence for audits, with Security owning the control framework and this role owning control execution for infrastructure.
Support computer system validation (CSV/CSA) for GxP-relevant infrastructure, along with change control and audit readiness.
Lead infrastructure responses during internal, customer, and regulatory audits.
Protect patient health information through appropriate data residency, encryption, access controls, and logging.

Resilience, Operations & Service Management

Own business continuity and disaster recovery for infrastructure, with defined RTO/RPO targets for clinical and business-critical systems and regular DR testing.
Build observability, monitoring, and alerting practices using SRE principles, SLOs, and error budgets for critical services.
Mature ITSM processes for incident, problem, change, and configuration management using ITIL-aligned practices and tools such as ServiceNow.
Drive automation to reduce toil and improve reliability, speed, and consistency.

Vendor & Financial Management

Own the infrastructure budget across OpEx and CapEx, including forecasting, business cases, and cost optimization.
Manage strategic vendor, cloud provider, telecom, and managed service relationships, including contract negotiation and performance management.
Evaluate emerging technologies and make build, buy, or partner recommendations.

Technology Environment

Our environment spans enterprise infrastructure, cloud, networking, security, end-user computing, data, AI, and regulated clinical and manufacturing systems. Experience with every named technology is not required.

Cloud and platform: AWS, GCP, Azure, Microsoft 365, landing zones, Terraform or similar Infrastructure as Code, CI/CD, policy-as-code, containers, virtualization, and GPU infrastructure.
Netorking and connectivity: LAN/WAN, SD-WAN, Wi-Fi, SASE, DNS, load balancing, Direct Connect, Interconnect, private endpoints, VPN, transit architectures, NAC, firewalls, and WAF.
Data, AI, and analytics infrastructure: Snowflake, Databricks, enterprise AI and search platforms, ML/GPU workloads, private connectivity, and governed data products.
Security and identity: SSO, MFA, directory services, Zero Trust, endpoint management, vulnerability management, security telemetry, logging, and incident response integrations.
Operations and service management: observability, monitoring, SRE practices, SLOs, error budgets, backup and recovery, ServiceNow, ITIL, and disaster recovery testing.
Enterprise integrations and ecosystems: Jira, Confluence, GitLab, Salesforce, QAD, Workday, Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, and other business and clinical platforms.

Required Qualifications

15+ years of progressive experience in enterprise infrastructure, including 7+ years leading multi-disciplinary infrastructure teams at the director level or above.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Proven strength in ability to balance strategic vision with execution excellence, developing organizational capability while creating the capacity, accountability, and focus needed to consistently deliver on business and technology priorities.
Deep hands-on and architectural expertise in at least one major cloud platform, preferably AWS and/or GCP, with experience running multi-cloud and hybrid environments.
Strong background in enterprise networking and hands-on experience engineering and operating security infrastructure in partnership with a security organization.
Proven experience operating infrastructure in a regulated industry such as medical devices, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, or financial services.
Working knowledge of FDA regulations, including 21 CFR Part 11 and 21 CFR Part 820, as well as frameworks such as HIPAA, SOC 2, ISO 27001, and NIST CSF.
Track record of leading large-scale transformation programs, including cloud migration, data center consolidation, network modernization, or comparable enterprise initiatives.
Experience owning budgets of meaningful scale and managing strategic technology, cloud, telecom, and managed service vendors.
Excellent executive communication and influencing skills and the ability to translate technical risk, resilience, and investment into business outcomes.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in a medical device, digital health, or connected-device company supporting 24/7 clinical services.
Experience supporting manufacturing or OT networks and familiarity with IEC 62443 or similar OT security practices.
Familiarity with infrastructure for data and AI platforms, including Snowflake, Databricks, ML/GPU workloads, and enterprise AI tools.
Global infrastructure experience across the United States, United Kingdom/Europe, and Asia-Pacific, including data residency requirements.
Certifications such as AWS or GCP Professional Architect, CCIE/CCNP,
MBA or advanced degree.

Location:

Remote - US

Actual compensation may vary depending on job-related factors including knowledge, skills, experience, and work location.

Estimated Pay Range

$222,000.00 - $288,000.00
